answer: Originals are read in their pigment: hand-ground batches granulate unevenly, each session a density fingerprint, and pigment settles into the paper's hollows like snow filling tundra texture - pooling that interlocks only with its true ground. Every original registers its signature at its vertex, the focal point of densest pooling, and auditors re-wash margins under magnification: a copy on other terrain pools differently, machine-uniform where a hand-batch should stutter. Provenance is the interlock of grain and ground. Farms print flat, without stutter. Honest agents grind their own batches.
